sections.h2: Just how large is the county behind these tax bills?
sections.html:
Large enough to work as several markets at once. QuickFacts lists these headline numbers:

  • Land area: 1,899.90 square miles.
  • Mid-2025 population estimate: 2,802,029.
  • Housing units: 1,125,274, of which 52.2 percent are lived in by their owners.
  • Typical owned home, 2020 to 2024: $463,000.
  • Household income in that span: $71,753, in 2024 dollars.

Nearly half of households rent, and the distance between home prices and paychecks explains why caps and exemptions get so much attention here.

sections.h2: Who do I call first about a Miami-Dade tax question?
sections.html:
Match the question to the desk. Three county offices split the job.

  • Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, portability and classifications. The main office is in the Stephen P. Clark Center, 111 NW 1st Street, Suite 710 (305-375-4712). The Cutler Bay branch is at 10710 SW 211 Street, 2nd Floor (305-232-3810). Each is staffed on weekdays during business hours.
  • Tax Collector: prints and collects the bill, with 13 service locations, 24 hour online payment and mobile offices that visit neighborhoods.
  • Clerk of the Courts: records deeds, takes value petitions and runs tax deed auctions.

The appraiser says outright that it does not send tax bills and does not set or collect taxes, so a gripe about the size of a bill is really a question for the taxing bodies that levy millage.

sections.h2: How did the 2026 Miami-Dade roll take shape?
sections.html:
The appraiser published a June 1 estimate of $540.7 billion in countywide taxable value, a 5.5 percent rise on 2025 and 3.2 percentage points slower than the year before. Estimates guide city and county budget planning; they are not final.

A July 1 preliminary certification followed. Then the County Commission ordered the roll extended on September 1, 2026, and the appraiser certified it on October 16, 2026. That certification is the first one, before any changes the Value Adjustment Board makes after appeals.

2026 roll steps posted by the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser
StepWhat the appraiser reports
June 1 estimate$540.7 billion taxable, up 5.5%
July 1Preliminary certification sent to taxing authorities
September 1, 2026County Commission orders the roll extended
October 16, 2026Initial certification of the full roll

Source: Property Appraiser of Miami-Dade County.

sections.h2: Why can two Miami-Dade neighbors pay such different rates?
sections.html:
Because the total comes from stacked taxing bodies, and the city layer varies widely. The appraiser's 2026 millage chart runs from 14.9007 on one North Miami Beach line to 24.1893 in Biscayne Park, with unincorporated areas at 16.8983.

Other totals on the chart: Miami 19.9544, Miami Beach 18.6681, Hialeah 18.6134, Coral Gables 18.1518 and Doral 16.9487. Some rows add debt service or special district lines, which is why you should match your own address to a row rather than quote a city figure.

Separate tax guides cover Miami and Miami Beach.

sections.h2: Which cities sit at the low and high ends of the chart?
sections.html:
The chart lists more than three dozen taxing areas, from Aventura, Bal Harbour and Bay Harbor Islands through Key Biscayne, Pinecrest, Sunny Isles Beach and Surfside to West Miami, plus the unincorporated area. Looking only at each city's own operating line:

  • Lowest: Doral at 1.5994 mills, Sunny Isles Beach at 1.6514, Aventura at 1.7261.
  • Middle: Homestead at 5.9604, Hialeah at 6.3018, Miami Gardens at 6.9363.
  • Highest: Biscayne Park at 9.2000, Opa-locka at 8.9797, El Portal at 8.0500.

A low city line can still sit on a heavy total once school, county, fire and library lines are added. Read the bottom number.

sections.h2: What does the county's economy add to the roll?
sections.html:
Census data for 2023 count 98,394 employer establishments with 1,055,440 employees and about $71.6 billion in annual payroll, a 4.6 percent employment gain on 2022. For 2022 the Census lists $67.1 billion in retail sales, $15.4 billion in lodging and food service, $30.3 billion in health care receipts and $38.5 billion in transportation and warehousing. Permits issued in 2025 numbered 16,535.

Businesses carry their own bill. Owners of furniture, equipment and similar property file Form DR-405 with the appraiser by April 1, and the appraiser runs a lookup for tangible property by business name, address or folio.

sections.h2: When is the Miami-Dade bill due, and what does paying early save?
sections.html:
Bills land in November, and the best discount, 4 percent, belongs to that month alone. It steps down by a point each month to 1 percent in February, and anything unpaid on April 1 is delinquent. The tax collector promotes the November discount with a "Save the Max" campaign and takes payment online, at its 13 locations or at its mobile offices.

  • August: the proposed-tax notice previews the bill.
  • Twenty-five days from that notice: the last chance for a value petition at the clerk's desk.
  • Thirty days after a denial letter is mailed: the window to challenge an exemption denial.
  • May 1: the cutoff for asking the collector for installments.

sections.h2: What happens when a Miami-Dade bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid balances turn into tax certificates, which the collector auctions to whoever will accept the lowest interest, bidding down in quarter-point steps. Certificates nobody bids on pass to the county at the top rate, and the sales wrap up by June 1. A homestead parcel owing less than $250 skips the auction and goes to the county. The collector retains a 5 percent commission.

Deed pressure comes slowly: a holder must wait out two years from the April after issue, then pay a $75 application charge. At the later auction the top bidder posts a deposit of 5 percent or $200, whichever is larger, and settles the rest inside 24 hours on business days. The tax collector lists a Tax Certificate Sales service; ask the clerk about auction dates.

sections.h2: How fast can a Miami-Dade assessment climb?
sections.html:
Homestead value is held to the smaller of 3 percent and inflation. Rentals, second homes and commercial parcels face a 10 percent annual ceiling. A sale wipes out both cushions, since the new owner is assessed at market the following January 1.

A constitutional amendment that voters approved in November 2026 is already built into the appraiser's estimator, which shows Amendment 3 figures for 2027 and 2028. Run your own folio through it before guessing at a future bill. Millage itself still comes out of budget hearings held in the fall.

sections.h2: Which breaks can a Miami-Dade homeowner claim?
sections.html:
The base homestead exemption reaches $50,000 and is claimed with the appraiser by March 1. Other breaks target particular owners.

  • Seniors: an added amount of up to $50,000 where a local ordinance provides it and household income stays under the cap.
  • Service-connected disability at 10 percent or higher: a $5,000 reduction.
  • Older veterans with a permanent service-connected disability: a discount equal to the VA rating.
  • Deferral: file Form DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31 to postpone the share of the bill above 5 percent of income, or 3 percent for permanent residents past 65.

sections.h2: Can the appraiser's online tools save me a trip?
sections.html:
Often. Widow(er) exemptions and disability exemptions for veterans or surviving spouses can be filed online, and agricultural classification uses form MD-482 with uploaded papers. Appointments can be booked online, and a tax estimator and walkthrough video sit on the home page.

Two protections stand out. The clerk runs a free alert that pings an owner within a day when a deed or mortgage is filed under that name, and the appraiser's compliance team takes suspected homestead fraud reports at 305-375-3402.

sections.h2: What changes in the tax bill when a Miami-Dade house sells?
sections.html:
The title agent asks the collector for a payoff figure and settles the year's tax at the closing table, divided as the contract says. The buyer arrives with a reassessed value and needs a fresh exemption filing.

Deed stamps here are set at 60 cents per $100, and the county adds a 45 cent surtax per $100 that state revenue officials exclude for a deed conveying only a single-family dwelling. Ask the closing agent which line fits your deed.

faqs.q: What total millage applies in unincorporated Miami-Dade for 2026?
faqs.a: The chart total is 16.8983 mills. That is the combined figure for the unincorporated area; incorporated cities have their own totals.

faqs.q: Where can a Miami-Dade owner pay the bill?
faqs.a: Use the Tax Collector: its website, any of 13 locations or a visiting mobile office. The appraiser takes no payments.

faqs.q: How soon must a Miami-Dade value petition be filed?
faqs.a: Twenty-five days from the August notice of proposed taxes. File the petition with the clerk. A denied exemption follows a 30 day clock from the letter.

faqs.q: Does paying early cut a Miami-Dade bill?
faqs.a: Yes, by up to 4 percent. The reduction shrinks every month from November and is gone by March.

faqs.q: Is Miami-Dade subject to the Save Our Homes limit?
faqs.a: Yes. Homestead growth is limited to the lesser of 3 percent or inflation, and a sale resets it.
